title: Symmetric Bead Strand
story: A jewellery maker designs bracelets in a web app. Each bead is a node holding a color code, linked to the next bead. The app can only walk the strand forwards from the clasp.
Some customers want a symmetric bracelet: the same read from either end. The app checks each order, and its device is short on memory, so it should not copy the strand.
task: Write isSymmetric(head). Return true if the sequence of values in the linked list reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise false.
An empty strand and a single bead both count as symmetric. Aim for O(n) time and O(1) extra memory. You may change the links while you work.

examples.explanation: Read from either end you get 3, 7, 5, 7, 3. The middle bead, 5, pairs with itself.
The middle two beads match, but the ends are 3 and 4. Read backwards the strand is 4, 7, 7, 3, which is different.

hints: In an array you would compare first with last, second with second-to-last, and so on. What stops you here?
You cannot walk backwards from the far end. But if the second half pointed the other way, you could walk inwards from both ends.
Two tools you may know: finding the middle with slow and fast pointers, and reversing a list in place.

Find the middle with slow/fast pointers. Reverse the list from slow onward. Walk one pointer from head and one from the reversed half's head, comparing values, until the reversed half runs out. Any mismatch means false.
bruteForce: Copy every color code into an array and compare with two indexes moving in from both ends, or push every value on a stack and compare while popping.
Both are O(n) time but also O(n) extra memory for a full copy. O(1) extra memory means working on the links themselves.

walkthrough: A singly linked list cannot walk backwards, so reverse the second half in place, then compare from both ends.
• Find the middle. slow/fast go 3/3, then 7/5, then 5/3. fast.next is null, so slow stops on 5.
• Reverse from 5 onward: 5 → 7 → 3 becomes 3 → 7 → 5. The first half still runs 3 → 7 → 5, because 7 still points to 5.
• Compare: left 3 vs right 3, left 7 vs right 7, left 5 vs right 5. The reversed half ends. Every pair matched, so return true.

Loop on right, the reversed half, not on left. For an odd length the middle node is in both halves and is compared with itself, which is harmless. Real code would reverse the second half back afterwards, with the same loop, so the caller gets the strand unchanged.
solution.timeWhy: Three passes, each over at most the whole list.
solution.spaceWhy: Only a few pointers; the reversal reuses the existing nodes.
solution.takeaway: Harder linked list problems are often several small techniques combined. This one uses fast and slow pointers to find the middle, in-place reversal of the second half, and then two pointers walking towards each other.
